newsitem.title: UK: Uneven copper product demand in Europe, exports up.
newsitem.headline: Uneven copper product demand in Europe, exports up.

text.p: Demand for copper products in Europe is patchy, but strong overseas consumption and weak local currencies have boosted exports, industry sources said.
As copper futures touched a fresh one-year high of $2,530 a tonne on the London Metal Exchange on Thursday, supplies of raw copper remained tight, most fabricator sources said.
"The demand side is a mixed picture really," said one industry source in Britain.
Overall consumption in Europe is up modestly, but there are big variations between countries and type of product.
One particularly soft area for cable demand has been Italy, where the privatisation of utilities has hit the market, the British source added.
In France, a spokeswoman for Alcatel Cable said the European copper cable market declined last year, but did not give any figures.
"The company does not expect an increase in European cable demand in 1997," she added, referring to all types of cable.
Alcatel Cable controls 22 percent of the European cable and wire market.
But rod mills on the continent were going full force, industry sources said.
"Our sales of copper rod and semi-fabricated products have been encouraging in a competitive environment," said Werner Marnette, chairman of German refiner Norddeutsche Affinerie AG (NA).
Sales were particularly strong in Asia and exports have been helped by a favourable currency equation, he added.

Industry sources said other fabricators were also exploiting export opportunities linked to the sharp rise of the dollar since the beginning of the year, because products priced in local currencies are now cheaper.
The dollar against the mark surged to a peak of nearly 1.74 from 1.54 since January and the franc to 5.86 from 5.20.
"They have been selling to the Middle East, India, Pakistan, Taiwan and Korea, which are pretty exotic destinations for Europe," one source said.
Another industry source, based in Germany, said: "Demand for processed copper products is stable in Europe but exceptionally good in the Far East and the United States."
The rod business depends on high volumes and the currency moves have given these firms additional flexibility to lock in good margins, sources said.
"The question is how long will this continue," a British source added.
Regarding the supply of raw copper to fabricators, the spot market was genuinely tight, most sources said.
Norddeutsche's Marnette said the tightness was exacerbated by short supplies of Russian material.
In Britain, which depends heavily on imports, there have been several shipment delays from Chile and also some instances where tonnages were switched.
Some players have made misjudgements on spot premiums, holding off from agreeing contracts for the full year since they expected a surplus to pressure premiums, one source said.
But the Alcatel spokeswoman said the group has had no difficulties in finding copper despite the tight stocks and surging prices.
"For us prices and supplies are not linked. We have had no problems to secure copper," she said.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
